title: Introduction and overview — F-4 Phantom II
description: Signature-original re-engineering study: introduction and overview of the F-4 Phantom II. This is a Signature-original design study, explicitly labeled and never presented as public record. Baseline reference: Twin-engine two-seat fighter; 5,195 built by McDonnell Douglas; main U.S. fighter of the Vietnam era.. The F-4 Phantom II is a twin-engine, two-seat fighter built by McDonnell Douglas, first flown in 1958 and the principal U.S. fighter of the Vietnam War era. A total of 5,195 were built, serving the U.S. Navy, Marine Corps, and Air Force plus eleven allied nations. It set 16 world speed, altitude, and time-to-climb records. Signature improvements explored here: Signature composite primary structures cut empty weight ~12% versus the public baseline; Signature avionics suite with predictive-maintenance health monitoring on every major system.
